Name: Fashion Sense - Wardrobe Manager
Author: NatrollEXE
Description:
[left][b][color=#c27ba0][size=5]Description[/size][/color][/b][/left]
[left]This mod adds a small preview window and a button to expand the preview in the Fashion Sense saved outfits menu, so you can see how an outfit looks before equipping it.[/left]

[left]I originally made this mod for personal use because I had a lot of saved outfits and kept getting lost while trying to find a specific one. Fashion Sense shows outfit names but does not provide a visual preview in the saved outfits list, so I wanted a way to check the look before equipping it.[/left]

[left]After making it work, I thought it might be useful for other players too, so I decided to share it.[/left]

[left][size=5][b][color=#c27ba0] [/color][color=#c27ba0]> [/color][color=#ffffff]> [/color][color=#c27ba0]> [/color][color=#ffffff]> [/color][color=#c27ba0]> [/color][color=#ffffff]> [/color][color=#c27ba0]> [/color][color=#ffffff]> [/color][color=#c27ba0]> [/color][color=#ffffff]> [/color][color=#c27ba0]> [/color][color=#ffffff]> [/color][color=#c27ba0]> [/color][color=#ffffff]> [/color][color=#c27ba0]> [/color][color=#ffffff]> [/color][color=#c27ba0][u]Updates[/u][/color][color=#ffffff] ! [/color][color=#c27ba0][size=5]<[/size][/color][color=#ffffff] < [/color][color=#c27ba0]< [/color][color=#ffffff]< [/color][color=#c27ba0]< [/color][color=#c27ba0]< [/color][color=#ffffff]< [/color][color=#c27ba0]< [/color][color=#ffffff]< [/color][color=#c27ba0]< [/color][color=#ffffff]< [/color][color=#c27ba0]< [/color][color=#ffffff]< [/color][color=#c27ba0]< [/color][color=#ffffff]< [/color][color=#c27ba0]< [/color][color=#ffffff]< [/color][color=#c27ba0]< [/color][/b][/size][/left]
[left]Over time, I kept adding new features to make large outfit collections easier to manage, including categories, tags, advanced filters, outfit management tools, and automatic outfit schedules. At that point, the mod was no longer focused only on previewing outfits, so its original name no longer represented everything it had become.[/left]
[left]For that reason, starting with version 1.0.7, I decided to rename it [b][color=#c27ba0]Fashion Sense - Wardrobe Manager[/color][/b]. It is still the same project and continues to include the original preview features, but the new name better reflects its broader purpose as an in-game wardrobe companion for Fashion Sense.[/left]

[left][color=#c27ba0][size=5][b]Installation Instructions[/b][/size][/color][/left]
[list=1]
[*]Install SMAPI.[/*]
[*]Install Fashion Sense.[/*]
[*]Download this mod.[/*]
[*]Extract the folder into your Stardew Valley Mods folder.[/*]
[*]Launch the game through SMAPI.[/*]
[/list]
[left][color=#c27ba0][size=5][b]How to Use[/b][/size][/color][/left]
[list]
[*]Open the saved outfits menu in Fashion Sense.[/*]
[*]Click the [b]Expand[/b] button to open the full outfit browser.[/*]
[*]Browse your outfits in a larger interface with a live preview of your farmer on the right.[/*]
[/list][left]You can also hold [b]CTRL[/b] and left-click an outfit for a quick preview without opening the expanded menu.[/left]

[left]Note: The configured preview shortcut is always used together with the left mouse button.[/left]
[left][color=#ffffff]Designed to make large Fashion Sense clothing collections easier to browse, especially for players with hundreds of saved looks ([/color][b][color=#c27ba0]like me, LOL[/color][color=#ffffff]).[/color][/b][/left]

[b][color=#ffffff][img]https://i.imgur.com/3fVa5wi.gif[/img][/color][/b]

[color=#c27ba0][size=5][b]Automatic Outfit Schedules[/b][/size][/color]
[color=#ffffff]The expanded outfit browser also includes a fully visual scheduler that can automatically change your saved Fashion Sense outfits. No JSON editing or special outfit naming convention is required.
Use the seasonal and schedule tabs on the left side of the expanded browser:[/color]

[list]
[*][color=#ffffff]Spring, Summer, Fall, and Winter — rules created inside these tabs only apply during their respective season.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffffff]Festivals — create rules for vanilla festivals and optionally show festivals added by other mods.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffffff]Daily — general everyday rules that can work during any season.[/color][/*]
[/list][b][color=#c27ba0][size=5]Creating a schedule[/size][/color][/b]
[list=1]
[*][color=#ffffff]Open one of the schedule tabs.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffffff]Click “New schedule”.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffffff]Choose the conditions you want to use.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffffff]Click “Select outfits” and choose one or more saved Fashion Sense outfits.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffffff]Leave the schedule enabled and confirm your selection.[/color][/*]
[/list][color=#ffffff]Depending on the selected tab, a schedule can use:[/color]

[list]
[*][color=#ffffff]All days, one specific day, or multiple days from 1 to 28.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffffff]One or multiple weather conditions.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffffff]Any time period, morning, afternoon, or night.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffffff]One or multiple exact times. Exact times are optional.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffffff]One or multiple locations, including the Farmhouse, indoor or outdoor locations, and a selection of vanilla areas.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffffff]A specific festival or multiple festivals.[/color][/*]
[/list][color=#ffffff]Conditions selected in the same schedule work together. For example, you can create a Spring schedule for day 14, during nighttime, inside the Farmhouse, at 10:00 PM.
The scheduler checks your rules when a save is loaded, when a new day begins, when the player changes location, and as the in-game clock changes.[/color]

[b][color=#c27ba0][size=5]Selecting outfits, categories, and tags[/size][/color][/b]
[color=#ffffff]The outfit selection window can be used in two different ways:[/color]

[list]
[*][color=#ffffff]Use categories, tags, and color tags as filters, then manually select only the outfits you want for that schedule.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffffff]Select “Whole tag” to use an entire tag as a dynamic outfit group.[/color][/*]
[/list][color=#ffffff]A dynamic tag always uses the outfits currently assigned to it. For example, if a schedule uses the whole “Green” color tag, any outfit you later add to that tag automatically becomes available to the schedule.
You can combine individually selected outfits with one or more dynamic tags. Duplicate outfits are removed automatically.
If multiple valid outfits are available, the scheduler chooses one at random whenever that rule is activated or reevaluated.[/color]

[b][color=#c27ba0][size=5]Schedule priority[/size][/color][/b]
[color=#ffffff]When more than one schedule matches:[/color]
[list]
[*][color=#ffffff]Festival schedules have the highest priority.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffffff]Seasonal schedules come next.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffffff]Daily schedules act as general fallback rules.[/color][/*]
[/list][color=#ffffff]More specific rules, such as a particular day or schedules with additional conditions, are prioritized over broader rules in the same section.
Schedules are stored separately for each save file and can be enabled, disabled, edited, or deleted from the visual interface.[/color]

[b][color=#c27ba0][size=5]Indoor Outfit Adjustments[/size][/color][/b]
Want to leave your raincoat’s umbrella outside? You can choose which Fashion Sense hat and accessories from a saved outfit should be hidden indoors, without creating a second outfit.
[list=1]
[*]Open the expanded outfit browser.[/*]
[*]Right-click the saved outfit and select Indoor Adjustments.[/*]
[*]Select the hat or accessories you want to hide, then click Save.[/*]
[*]Add that outfit to an automatic outfit schedule.[/*]
[/list]When the schedule equips the outfit, the selected pieces are hidden inside buildings and restored when you go outdoors. You can select more than one accessory. 🩷

[b][color=#c27ba0][size=5]Important Notes and Compatibility[/size][/color][/b]
[list]
[*][color=#ffffff]A schedule needs at least one valid saved outfit or a dynamic tag containing outfits. If a selected tag is empty, the schedule remains saved but cannot change the farmer’s outfit until an outfit is assigned to that tag.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffffff]If an outfit used by a schedule is deleted, it will no longer be available to that rule. Dynamic tags automatically follow their current outfit assignments.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffffff]Festival schedules have the highest priority, followed by seasonal schedules. Daily schedules work as general fallback rules.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffffff]When two rules from the same section match, the more specific rule takes priority. A rule using a specific day, weather, period, location, festival, or exact time is considered more specific than a broad rule.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffffff]Weather Wonders has direct built-in support, including its additional weather conditions.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffffff]Weather types added by other mods are also supported. Unknown custom weather IDs can be detected when that weather is active and then selected and saved in a schedule.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffffff]Custom active and passive festivals can optionally be displayed in the festival selector.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffffff]Automatic outfit mods may conflict if more than one tries to equip an outfit at the same time.[/color][/*]
[/list][color=#c27ba0][size=5][b]Another Automatic Outfit Option[/b][/size][/color]
[color=#ffffff]If you prefer a ready-made automatic outfit system based on outfit naming conventions and predefined situations, please also check out [b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/38381]Auto-change Outfits by ahomiepassingby[/url].[/b]

Since both mods can automatically change Fashion Sense outfits, using both automation systems at the same time may cause them to compete over which outfit should be equipped. To avoid unexpected outfit changes, use only one automatic outfit system at a time.[/color]
